Today, Apple is celebrating the opening of its Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston, Texas. Here are the details.

Apple to provide training for business leaders at its newly opened Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston

Apple today opened its new Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston. The center provides free training and educational courses for small and medium-sized businesses, giving them hands-on access to the most advanced equipment, interactive labs, and various tools to accelerate innovation. The Advanced Manufacturing Center is located in the same Houston facility that produces and ships Apple's advanced AI servers, and will begin producing the Mac mini later this year.⋯⋯ Apple CEO Tim Cook said: "In just nine short months, we have invested hundreds of millions of dollars in this Houston facility. We have built the factory, begun production, and have already shipped the first advanced AI servers from this plant. Today we are delighted to open this new Advanced Manufacturing Center, which will be a place where business leaders, workers, and students can learn the same innovative processes we use to manufacture Apple's most groundbreaking products. We also look forward to beginning production of the Mac mini later this year. We believe in the strength of American workers and American creativity, and we are moving forward at an extraordinary pace because what we want to create is not just great products — what we want to build is the future of American manufacturing."

Tim Cook announced his trip to Houston through social media, making a special trip to attend the opening ceremony. Guests attending the launch ceremony included U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, Houston Mayor John Whitmire, U.S. Congressman Christian Menefee, and Harris County Precinct One Commissioner Rodney Ellis.

The Advanced Manufacturing Center covers 20,000 square feet, where Apple's experts will "directly share their knowledge with participating businesses and entrepreneurs to help accelerate the development of American intelligent manufacturing."

The first group of business leaders arrived today to attend the inaugural training session. The day's topics centered on intelligent manufacturing technologies, including "machine learning-driven quality control and advanced automation."
